title: Military modernization and operational demand can coexist with readiness and sustainment gaps
source_unit: GAO-26-108888, Military Readiness: DOD Should Take Further Actions to Address Challenges Across the Air, Sea, Ground, and Space Domains
geography: United States Department of Defense; air, sea, ground, and space readiness evidence summarized from GAO work since 2022

observations.period: GAO readiness work summarized in March 2026

denominator.unit: approximately the number of GAO recommendations across the readiness reports summarized; more than 150 still required additional DOD action

availability_goals.unit: DOD current-force availability goals for aircraft, ships, vehicles, and personnel required to operate and maintain them

sustainment.unit: maintenance, logistics, repair, personnel, training, and data problems across domains

quality_of_life.value: poor housing and fatigue identified as readiness factors
quality_of_life.unit: reported personnel and institutional conditions affecting readiness

observations.method: GAO testimony synthesizing published readiness, operations, maintenance, personnel, and training reviews across the military services, with interviews of responsible officials.
observations.uncertainty: This is a cross-report oversight synthesis, not one common readiness denominator or a new causal estimate. Availability measures differ by service and system; classified information and ongoing work are not fully visible in the public testimony.
observations.subgroup: Air, sea, ground, and space domains; military services and readiness functions differ in goals, measures, and constraints.
observations.counterinterpretation: A readiness gap in one fleet or function does not mean the entire force is unusable. Some recommendations may be implemented after the testimony, and operational risk depends on mission, location, substitution, allies, and time horizon.

denominator.unit: Army watercraft in the fleet discussed by GAO

fully_mission_capable_rate_2020.unit: percent of Army watercraft fleet fully mission capable in 2020

fully_mission_capable_rate_2024.unit: percent of Army watercraft fleet fully mission capable in 2024

policy_goal.unit: percent fully mission capable goal identified in Army policy for ground equipment including watercraft

observations.method: GAO summary of Army watercraft readiness and maintenance findings, including fleet size, mission-capable rates, maintenance delays, handwritten maintenance systems, and governance gaps.
observations.uncertainty: The watercraft series is one fleet example and does not represent all Army or DOD equipment. A mission-capable rate is not the same as combat effect, availability at the point of need, crew readiness, or partner contribution.
observations.subgroup: Army watercraft fleet used for transport, exercises, and humanitarian missions, including Indo-Pacific requirements.
observations.counterinterpretation: Modernization or acquisition could change future readiness, and the reported rate does not show whether other assets substituted for watercraft missions or how operational priorities changed.

related_sources.claim: GAO product page identifies the testimony, scope, and publication details for the military-readiness synthesis.

boundary: This record shows a readiness-conversion problem: military activity, modernization, and strategic demand can coexist with maintenance, personnel, quality-of-life, data, and availability gaps. It does not establish overall military weakness, deterrence failure, combat performance, ally willingness, or an attributed geopolitical outcome.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: GAO public testimony HTML report retrieved and hashed; underlying service readiness data and classified reports not retained
